# RCHub Plugins

> New authoring model: native application installed from a public GitHub repository URL. Twelve official Windows x64 native packages (version 1.0.0) are published in `plugins/official-native` and served by a compatible host's authenticated V2 catalog; production native capability is still fail-closed because cross-process owner invalidation is not covered, and Linux packages are not published. Legacy V1 Wasm support, imports and catalog paths have not yet been technically removed.

## Start here

- [English developer guide](docs/plugins/README.md) and [Türkçe geliştirici rehberi](docs/plugins/README.tr.md): developer workflow, installation and security.
- [Published official native packages](plugins/official-native/README.md): twelve Windows x64 packages, version 1.0.0, with exact artifact SHA-256 values.
- [Native ABI2 contract](contracts/plugins/v2/README.md): schema, IPC and semantic requirements; descriptor schemaVersion 2, authenticated wire v3/version 2 and negotiated IPC version 2 are distinct.
- [Native example EN/TR](plugins/examples/application-v2/README.md): local illustrative Windows example; it is not one of the published official packages.
- [Preparation CLI](tools/plugins/rchub_app_v2_cli.py): prepare binds a template to supplied native bytes; verify checks the binding. Neither builds, publishes, installs, executes or approves the application.
- [Python protocol module](tools/plugins/rchub_app_v2.py), [application schema](contracts/plugins/v2/application.schema.json), [IPC schema](contracts/plugins/v2/protocol.schema.json), [transport schema](contracts/plugins/v2/transport.schema.json).

## Published official packages

All twelve are MIT-licensed, target `windows-x86_64`, use entry `bin/rchub-official-native.exe` and permission `native.unsandboxed`, and sit in `plugins/official-native/<directory>/` as complete package roots (`rchub-app.json`, artifact, `native-source.json`, `native-runtime/` sources and lockfile, `LICENSE`, README).

| Directory | ID | Version | Artifact SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apps` | `com.rchub.apps` | 1.0.0 | `ec04c89844a79e25aff04655ddf6e681a3e6abd093afa82e3b0cc206e639c8f1` |
| `audio` | `com.rchub.audio` | 1.0.0 | `db6d24b13cfec4fb3555e110634d298f04dc65540398219606d039cadea5d49a` |
| `browser` | `com.rchub.browser` | 1.0.0 | `4a114f702da7ac1c994554739d8a25b3056d03b95d6fa311bd54f08fd7247810` |
| `clipboard` | `com.rchub.clipboard` | 1.0.0 | `2137e5fb94be53a6dc2baeaeede7c37b2b93113b0bcb57665aec87be3ce3234a` |
| `display` | `com.rchub.display` | 1.0.0 | `05f4590cd76206a95ce83b33cfc6127af528ed0ba4bf249df58de1556a42f60d` |

| `speech` | `com.rchub.speech` | 1.0.0 | `4de8591d6a86b92614b35339fe2d9173109f1aa93286dc7e1ea5f4d50556afe3` |
| `system` | `com.rchub.system` | 1.0.0 | `7fc767a4cc8fccd1c50f63f4510c295f1d1b34bcba3b1caeb3c910e8de465585` |

The host serves them from its own `plugins/official-native` checkout through `GET /api/plugins/v2/catalog` and `GET /api/plugins/v2/artifacts/<id>/<version>/<sha256>`. Both routes require authority: an account session Bearer token for mobile/web, or the paired-device `x-device-id`/`x-device-password` headers for the desktop; unauthorized requests get `401`, responses are non-cacheable, and the desktop catalog action stays disabled until it can send those credentials. The artifact route serves only bytes whose size and SHA-256 match the descriptor. Catalog listing and download are not installation, activation, publisher verification or proof of safety. This repository is a distribution catalog, not a per-package repository root: the GitHub-URL resolver requires `rchub-app.json` at a repository root, so these monorepo subdirectory URLs cannot be installed through it.

## Author and install your own repository

1. Implement framed IPC and declared actions, events and declarative surfaces against the ABI2 contract. Choose your own ID, version, reviewable source, license, EN/TR risk and data disclosures and `native.unsandboxed`; compile a real executable for the host target.
2. In your own repository place a validated descriptor named `rchub-app.json` at its root and the executable at the relative `execution.artifact.entry` path as a regular Git file. Set the artifact SHA-256 to the exact committed bytes. Manifest limit 64 KiB; artifact limit 16 MiB. Symlinks, submodules and Git LFS pointers are rejected.
3. Example for your own template and executable, from the developer-kit root:
   `python tools/plugins/rchub_app_v2_cli.py prepare --template template.json --artifact app.exe --target windows-x86_64 --entry app.exe --output rchub-app.json`
   `python tools/plugins/rchub_app_v2_cli.py verify --manifest rchub-app.json --artifact app.exe --target windows-x86_64 --entry app.exe`
4. Review code, binary, disclosures and license; commit descriptor and artifact to your repository's default branch, and make it public when ready. `https://github.com/<owner>/<repository>` is URL syntax only, not a published example. A compatible authenticated host with native capability and current authorized owner/device connection is required; production capability is currently disabled.
5. Enter that repository root URL in the native application workspace. HTTPS GitHub root URLs with optional `.git`/trailing slash are accepted, not branch or file URLs. The resolver pins the default branch commit, reads the root descriptor and artifact from that Git tree, verifies identity and SHA-256, and binds the download to the pinned commit and manifest hash. Resolution is not installation or publisher verification.
6. Review repository, commit, source, license, target, identity/hash, native permission and data behavior; explicitly approve installation on the available PC or phone. Installation stages bytes but does not activate them. Activate separately and open Controls. Authentication, ownership and exact grant checks remain in force; reconcile inventory before retrying an unknown outcome.

**Unsandboxed:** native code runs with normal user privileges and can access files, network and OS resources outside the broker. Hashes, source text, process boundaries and consent do not make untrusted binaries safe or verify their publisher. V1 grants do not transfer. Client/platform availability and live UI/authentication acceptance are not implied by this DEV workflow.

## Host wiring and boundaries

- Native V2 is included in default/release desktop builds; `plugin-dev-runtime` gates legacy Wasm development, not native V2. Production desktop builds require the build-time `RCHUB_SERVER_ORIGIN` to match the server's `RCHUB_PLUGIN_SERVER_ORIGIN` as a bare HTTPS origin; missing or invalid configuration fails closed. Loopback HTTP is for development only.
- `ownerInvalidationCovered` covers audited same-process mutations, not immediate changes via direct SQL, admin or other processes. Missing coverage or owner reader disables native readiness and dispatch. Production deliberately disables coverage, so native capability is unavailable there despite release wiring.
- In the RcHub host checkout, `tools/plugins/build_official_native.py` builds target bytes from `plugins/official/*/native-source.json` into `plugins/official-native/<name>/rchub-app.json` and its artifact by default. The host server reads `plugins/official-native` relative to its working directory or parent and exposes `/api/plugins/v2/catalog` and hash-bound artifact paths, and omits missing/invalid entries. This sibling repository publishes the same layout for Windows x64. Serving a catalog entry is not publisher verification, installation or safety.
- The RcHub official native builder preserves its checked-in `Cargo.lock` and builds with Cargo `--locked`; it fails if the lockfile is missing or inconsistent.
- For official native batch builds, `--repositories` accepts a JSON map of every package supported by the selected platform to its actual public repository URL; existing output directories are never overwritten. Building is not publication.
- Live DB/JWT, visible UI, full production deployment and Linux acceptance remain unverified. Synthetic DB, injected transport and headless evidence are not release acceptance.

## Historical compatibility

The [legacy V1 contract](contracts/plugins/README.md), SDK and old packages remain in this checkout while technical removal is pending. They are not the recommended model for new development; the published native packages above are catalog-distributed, not V1-compatible replacements, and V1 grants never transfer. [Provenance](plugins/examples/application-v2/PROVENANCE.md) records the scope and limitations of earlier local asset work.
